factor_diagnostics.value_notes: A southeastern Gulf study reports that sea-surface temperature influences red grouper abundance and that thermal relationships differ between juveniles and adults. The Gulf States Marine Fisheries Commission life-history table reports juvenile occurrence at 16.1–31.2 °C and larval optimum estimates of 27.4–28.5 °C. These are stage-specific and regional observations, not a validated adult South Florida SST preference curve; they do not establish the configured 18–28 °C range or 21–25 °C ideal.
